add.issue.name: xlint: check final newline in .md files

edit.description.md:
## Problem

`check_final_newline` runs only in the `.py` branch of `check_file` in `tools/xlint/xlint.py`. A `.md` file gets exactly one check (space indentation), so a missing final newline in Markdown is invisible to xlint.

Hit live 2026-09-27: an edit silently dropped the trailing newline from `.agents/agent-notes-secretary-3.md`. Three sibling notes files all end with a newline, so it was a regression rather than house style — and xlint reported the file clean.

## Scope

- Apply `check_final_newline` to the `.md` branch, under the existing `--no-final-newline` flag.
- Respect the existing fence/frontmatter exemptions where relevant.

## Acceptance

- A `.md` missing its trailing newline fails; one with it passes.
- `--no-final-newline` disables the check for `.md` as it does for `.py`.
- Repo-wide `xlint $(git ls-files '*.md')` is clean, or every remaining finding is dispositioned.

## Notes

- **ai-ok**: an AI may pick this up and implement it without extensive discussion with the human.
- Related: GBNEWPS (frontmatter + fenced-code exemptions) is already implemented in `ed3d27e` but still sits in Todo — that ticket's status looks stale.
- Adjacent, deliberately *not* in scope: `check_trailing_whitespace` is also language-independent and is `.py`-only today. Worth its own ticket.

add.issue.name: Replace the broken coding subagent (mimo) — evaluate nemotron-3-ultra vs north-mini-code for quality

edit.description.md:
`opencode/mimo-v2.5-free` — the model AGENTS.md assigns to coding via `dispatch coding` — **fails instantly** with an opaque `UnknownError` ("Unexpected server error", ref `err_87964db6`, `err_0ac8beb6`). Tried twice on 2026-09-27, not transient; the process never starts. Coding work had to be run on `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` instead, which worked 3/3.

**The evaluation, per the human (2026-09-27):** compare quality of
- `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` — in effect **very cheap**: generous limits, *not*
  bundled into the same pool as big-pickle (unlike mimo and some others), and not
  in the OpenRouter free pool either. So mimo was effectively a *third* generous pool.
- `openrouter/cohere/north-mini-code:free` — a coding specialist (30B MoE, 3B active,
  256K ctx, quality 24). Currently referenced in 5 agent files: `mechanic.md`,
  `programmer.md`, `overseer.md`, `worker-mimo.md`, `worker-north-mini-code.md`.

**Cost asymmetry to weigh:** north-mini-code sits on the **shared OpenRouter `:free`
pool**, which AGENTS.md says to reserve for models with no console equivalent. When
that daily pool hits zero every `:free` model returns empty and everything looks
broken. nemotron-ultra is on opencode's console gateway with generous limits. So
north-mini-code is not merely pricier in tokens — it is on a failure-prone pool.

**The deciding question is quality, because cheapness wins ties.** Cheapness per run
does not compensate for errors, so: given no meaningful change in quality, a cheaper
model is better. That makes this a quality comparison first and a cost comparison
second, with the pool-reliability difference as the tiebreak.

**Method note:** a real quality comparison needs a task with a known-correct answer
and scored output, not a vibe check. The cursor-reviewer-skill trials in
`/storage/cursor-review-baseline/` are the existing precedent for a scored,
frozen-subject comparison — reuse that shape rather than inventing one.

Also settle `programmer.md`'s model pin (see `WV26JZ2`, `3RVME3H`): it names
`worker-north-mini-code` while AGENTS.md's dispatch table says `worker-mimo`, and
the programmer is supposed to delegate coding to a worker anyway.

add.issue.name: Off-vocabulary categories in tasks.csv: research / ai-docs / personal (#61–#63, #65, #66)

edit.description.md:
Five open tasks carry category values that were never ruled on. All five appeared on 2026-09-27, all from the model-benchmark / codebase-comprehension work, and they are the only rows in the entire store that use them.

| # | category | task |
|---|----------|------|
| 61 | `research` | Model benchmark: widen the episode set |
| 62 | `ai-docs` | Correct library/ai/free-model-tier-list.md |
| 63 | `research` | Model benchmark: set G2–G5 thresholds |
| 65 | `personal` | Codebase comprehension learning process |
| 66 | `personal` | First 45-min comprehension block on mms-frontend |

## Why this needs a ruling, not a cleanup

The category column is the membership axis for project-scoped views (SPEC R4, Decision 8). A category only earns its place if some `.taskview.yaml` can scope to it or a pane can ask for it. `research` and `ai-docs` are neither a project nor a life area — they are *activities*. They name what the task is being done for, not what it is about, and that distinction is exactly what the human's rule turns on: **category = what the work is about, not which repo you are sitting in** (SPEC Decision 17).

The deeper problem is accretion. Nothing rejects a new category value, so the vocabulary grows one task at a time, by whoever happens to be in a session. A column that widens silently stops being a vocabulary. It is the same free-text drift already recorded for tags (`verif` vs `verify`), one level up and slower to notice.

## The specific questions

**#61, #62, #63 — model benchmark.** Three defensible answers, genuinely different:

- `work` — `TASKS.md` files the model benchmark under `### Work`.
- `XLib` — the harness lives at `$XLIB/tools/modelbench/`. Precedent: #56 (taskview project-specific) was labelled `XLib` even though its plan lives in the Agents repo, for exactly this reason.
- `Agents` — the plan is `Agents/plans/model-benchmark.md`, the output is `Agents/library/ai/models/`.

`#56` already set the precedent, so `XLib` is the consistent answer unless the human rules the benchmark is work rather than tooling.

**#65, #66 — codebase comprehension.** Almost certainly the same thing as `Personal Development`, spelled differently — `personal` vs `Personal Development` is the `verif`/`verify` drift again. `Personal Development` is the `TASKS.md` section name and is what #22, #23 and #41 were just labelled with in the 2026-09-27 pass, so these two are the odd ones out.

## Left unchanged on purpose

A live session owns this work. Relabelling under it would be invisible to whoever is mid-task and would make the pane disagree with the plan they are reading. Needs the human's ruling first, then one `taskupdate.py update <id> --category ...` per task.

add.issue.name: Agents AGENTS.md: `dispatch coding` routes to a big-pickle-pool worker, and worker-mimo pins a model the console dropped

edit.description.md:
`/storage/Agents/AGENTS.md` contradicts itself on the one rule that exists to protect the main model's quota.

- `:139` — "The main model (big-pickle / nemotron-3-ultra-free) is the primary rate-limit bottleneck — **preserve it by offloading** non-trivial work to subagents."
- `:143` — "**Coding / implementation** → `worker-mimo` (console `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free`). Strong coder; **use for coding by default**."
- `:173`, `:221`, `:247` repeat the `worker-mimo` routing (secretary pattern, programmer role, mechanic role).

`mimo` is **pool 1 — it shares big-pickle's quota** (topology in `/storage/Agents/.agents/shared-notes.md`, "Rate-limit pool topology (2026-09-27)"). So the default coding route spends the quota the line above it says to preserve, and it *is* the default: every dispatched coding task takes it.

**It is also self-refuting in practice.** `:141` tells agents to get the worker from `python3 $XLIB/tools/agent-coord.py dispatch <category>` — and that command's WORKER_MAP (`tools/agent-coord.py:540`) returns **`worker-north-mini-code`**. XLib's own AGENTS.md was already fixed this way (`8cb4daf`, plus the WORKER_MAP fix, both committed). The Agents file is the one left behind: `worker-mimo.md`'s description was already updated ("dispatch coding currently maps to worker-north-mini-code") and its parent doc was not.

**Second, mechanical defect — the pin is stale.** `worker-mimo.md` pins `opencode/mimo-v2.5-free`. `opencode models` (verified 2026-09-27) no longer lists v2.5; it lists **`opencode/mimo-v2.6-flash-free`**. A pin to a model the provider dropped is a dead worker behind a live name — the shared rule already says "ALWAYS verify with `opencode models` before pinning a model ID in an agent file".

**Fix, two parts:**

1. Re-point the four routing lines in `/storage/Agents/AGENTS.md` to `worker-north-mini-code` — or to whatever `9J30DNW` settles — so the doc matches the tool it tells agents to run, and coding stops defaulting into the protected pool.
2. Re-point `worker-mimo.md`'s `model:` to `mimo-v2.6-flash-free`, or delete the agent if nothing routes to it any more. Do not leave a broken pin.

**Related, not duplicate.** `9J30DNW` decides *which model codes best* (mimo fails outright; nemotron-3-ultra vs north-mini-code on quality, with the shared OpenRouter `:free` pool as the cost tiebreak). This ticket is the rule-level contradiction plus a stale pin, and it does not need that comparison settled. If `9J30DNW` picks the worker, part 1 collapses to a one-line edit.

add.issue.name: tasks.csv header declares 5 columns while every new row carries 8 — header-driven readers mis-map silently

edit.description.md:
Found while auditing taskview after the category/tag rollout (2026-09-27).

**The defect.** `~/.local/share/taskview/tasks.csv` carries the *old* header line:

    id,status,title,due_ts,chg_ts

but the schema is 8 columns (`// Schema:` comment line says so) and `ensure_csv` in `tools/taskview/taskupdate.py:20` writes 8 when it creates a file. It no-ops when the file already exists, so the on-disk header never self-heals. Field census of the live file: 63 rows with 5 fields, 48 with 8, 7 with 6, the rest wider (quoted titles containing commas — those parse fine).

**Why it matters.** `taskupdate.py` itself reads *positionally* (`row[5]`, guarded by `len(row) >`), so the tool is correct. The trap is any **header-driven** reader: `csv.DictReader` trusts that line and silently puts `category` under `due_ts` and shifts everything after. That already cost one session a whole table it was building for the human. A quiet wrong answer is worse than a crash.

**Fix options, pick one.**
- Repair the header on open (rewrite the field-name line, and migrate the 5-field rows to 8 so the file stops being mixed-format).
- Or drop the header line entirely and treat position 5-8 as optional — the readers already guard with `len(row) >`.
- Or leave the data alone and add a `taskupdate.py migrate` that reports the mixed format without writing.

**Definition of done.** A reader built on the header agrees with a positional reader for every id in the file, and there is a test that fails on the current file. Needs a spec line + tests per `XLib/doc/development.md` — taskview is committed (`250aaf1`), so this is real code, not scratch.

Related: the `tasks.csv` duplication between taskview and this board is `JM8GVW8`; vocabulary drift in the same file is `SNXBR23`.

add.issue.name: taskview pane shows no task id — a task can only be named by its truncated title

edit.description.md:
Found 2026-09-27, from the human: *"Referring to tasks by ID is convenient, but I don't have a quick reference right now."*

**The gap.** The tmux task pane renders title only — `truncate(current['title'], width - 2)` at `tools/taskview/taskview.py:371` for the current task, `:389` for the UPCOMING list. No id appears anywhere, so the pane cannot answer "which one is this?" Two titles sharing a first few words are indistinguishable, and truncated titles are worse.

Concrete symptom from this session: asked whether `#40` was the task about part switching, the only handle available was the number — the title had been truncated out of recognition.

**Proposed.** Prefix the id in both places, `#<id> ` before the title, and widen the truncation budget by the prefix width so the title does not get shorter. Formatting lives in the render layer, so this is presentation, not data.

**Half of a pair — read with `EY72YA9`.** Showing an id creates references, and right now resolving one means reading the CSV by hand, which is the exact failure mode `AQQNPAN` describes. Land the lookup (`EY72YA9`) with this, not after: an id in the pane that nothing can resolve is a worse gap than no id at all. The id prefix is nearly free on its own; the pair is what removes the "no quick reference" problem.

Raised by the human 2026-09-27 after a path sweep of the Agents workspace: *"As always, tracked files should not contain full system paths."* The rule had no written home and no mechanical check, so it kept slipping — 20 occurrences across 6 tracked files before this was cleaned by hand.

**Why it matters, twice over.** A tracked file is versioned *and* synced between machines, so an absolute path is wrong in the ordinary way (it means nothing on Dreamer, gab, Xena or the LXC) and in the git way (it records one machine's layout as if it were the project's). The designated home already exists: `.agents/machine-info.md` is git-ignored *precisely* so it can hold machine-specific facts. That makes this a layering rule with a known landing place, not a matter of taste.

**Proposed check.** In the `.md` branch, flag a path-like token that starts with `/storage/`, `/home/<user>/`, `/root/`, or `~/`. Message should name the file, the line, and the landing place: *point at `.agents/machine-info.md`, or make the path repo-relative.*

**Exemptions to design for, each with a reason** — a naive check would fire on all of these:

- `.agents/machine-info.md` itself, and anything git-ignored. It is the destination, not a violation. Detection has to be "is this file tracked", not "is it a `.md`".
- `AGENTS.md` setup walkthrough — `ln -s /path/to/XLib/tools …` and an `scp -r /storage/Agents/ …` example. The machine path is the *content* there.
- Plans that describe **another** machine's layout. `plans/remote-opencode-lxc.md` is six `/root/...` paths on the LXC host, and naming them is the document's subject.
- Paths quoted as **evidence**. A model-benchmark row quotes `/home/user/project/relative/path.py` — a fictional path a model copied verbatim, cited as proof of harness defect E9. It describes no real location.

That last pair is the honest hard part: the check cannot be "contains a slash-heavy token", it has to be a deliberate judgement about whether the path is *about* something or *about where something is*. Worth writing the exemptions into the spec rather than discovering them as false positives later.

**Process.** An xlint rule gets a plan doc under `XLib/doc/plans/` and tests, like the frontmatter/fence rule — see `GBNEWPS` for the shape and `XLib/doc/plans/xlint-frontmatter-fence-skip.md`. Same file and same one-deep `.md` branch as `GBNEWPS` and `PMRBFR3`; all three should be implemented together or at least not conflict.

Suggested spec line for the rule itself, if the human wants the convention written down as well as enforced — one line in `AGENTS.md`: *tracked files name paths relative to a repo, or point at `.agents/machine-info.md` for machine locations.* The check catches the symptom; the line explains it to the agent that writes the next file.

add.issue.name: bbprs.py: blocks_the_human() ignores `state`, so a PR where the human requested changes still reports BLOCKED ON YOU

edit.description.md:
## Symptom

`bbprs.py` reports a colleague's PR as `BLOCKED ON YOU`, and `--check` exits 1,
even after the human has **requested changes** on it. Confirmed 2026-09-30 on
`mms-frontend` #79 `profile_subscription`.

The human set `changes_requested` at 07:23 UTC. The tool still reported
`BLOCKED ON YOU` on a re-run at 07:23+ and again on a later run.

This is the **inverse of the truth**. Requesting changes *completes* your review
obligation and hands the ball to the author. The tool reports it as "I might be
blocking them", so it will keep sending the human to a PR that is not waiting on
them — until that PR is approved or declined.

## Root cause

`tools/bbprs/bbprs.py:143-158`

```python
def my_participation(self) -> str | None:
    for p in self.participants:
        if p.get("user", {}).get("nickname") == HUMAN:
            role = p.get("role", "?")
            return f"{role}/{'approved' if p.get('approved') else 'NOT approved'}"
    return None

def blocks_the_human(self) -> bool:
    if self.is_mine or self.draft:
        return False
    part = self.my_participation()
    return part is not None and part.endswith("/NOT approved")
```

`my_participation()` builds its string from the **boolean `approved` only**.
`state` is never read. Bitbucket sets `approved: false` for a
`changes_requested` participant, so "I asked for changes" and "I never looked at
it" produce the identical string `REVIEWER/NOT approved` — and
`blocks_the_human()` cannot tell them apart.

## Why it matters

This is the trap the tool's own README names: *"the trap most likely to make a
tool confidently wrong rather than fail."* It is a false positive on the one
question the tool exists to answer, and it is the kind that trains the human to
ignore a `--check` that genuinely matters. A false negative is at worst a wasted
look; this one is a standing instruction to go review a colleague's PR again.

## Fix

Distinguish the three reviewer states, not two:

- `state == "changes_requested"` → the human has done their part. **Not** blocked
  on them.
- approved → not blocked (already handled).
- neither → genuinely blocked on them.

Surface `state` in `my_participation()` so the rendered output says
`REVIEWER/changes_requested` rather than the misleading `NOT approved` — the

edit.description.md:
`epiq_issue_stats` on `ERZHM60` reads 0 commits / 0 files, though the change is committed as `d3f9b2b`. Every ticket whose subject matter is an agent file is unlinkable from this board.

Cause: `.opencode/agent/` is a symlink to `/storage/Agents/.opencode/agent` and is listed in XLib's `.gitignore`. Agent files are versioned in the **Agents** repo; this board's state branch lives in **XLib**. One board cannot span two repositories — link-by-reference matches commits reachable from the board's own repo, so an agent-file commit is invisible by construction. Compounding it, the commit subject carried no `ERZHM60` prefix, so it would not have matched even from the right board.

Already true of: `ERZHM60`, `3RVME3H`, `2YTGA0K`, `ACA67BQ`, `XS0KMB9`, `B26XEPM`, `Y2QYZV4`, `8GBDHGN`.

**The second board already exists** — `/storage/Agents/.epiq`, initialised 2026-09-27, board "Agents" (`91RTD68`). So this is not a tooling gap, it is a filing-location problem: agent-file tickets keep getting created on the XLib board.

Options:

1. **File agent-file tickets on the Agents board.** Zero new infrastructure, already half-adopted. Cost: a ticket that spans both repos (e.g. `AGENTS.md` + a role file) has no single home, and the XLib board stops being a complete picture of outstanding work.
2. **Track the agents dir from XLib** (real files instead of a symlink, or a submodule). One board, one link story. Cost: undoes a deliberate split — XLib's `.gitignore` names that path on purpose, and a submodule gives only a pointer commit, so per-ticket linking inside it still would not work.
3. **Enforce the prefix at least.** A pre-commit check in Agents rejecting `.opencode/agent/**` commits whose subject lacks a ref. Cheap, but a ref naming a board that cannot see the commit is worse than no ref — it looks linked and is not. Only worth doing alongside 1 or 2.
4. **Accept it and note it on the board**, so a zero-stats ticket is read as "lives in Agents" rather than "no work happened".

Recommend 1 plus 4: the split is deliberate, the second board is already there, and the failure mode to avoid is a stats-zero ticket that reads as untouched. Which is the human's call — option 2 in particular reverses a decision already written into `.gitignore`.
